summary.short: Virginia sales and use tax exemptions for commercial and industrial goods, including subdivisions 18–19 exempting data center computer equipment and software for operators meeting investment and job thresholds, from July 1, 2010 to June 30, 2035, with conditional extensions to 2040 or 2050.
summary.long: Section 58.1-609.3 of the Code of Virginia lists 21 commercial and industrial exemptions from the retail sales and use tax. Subdivisions 1 to 11, 16, 20 and 21 cover industrial materials, machinery, vessels, research, rail and airline property, meals, textiles, taxicab parts, beer brewing and advanced recycling; subdivision 2 excludes most electric power generation. Subdivisions 12 and 13 cover oil, gas and spaceport activities, and subdivisions 14 and 15 cover semiconductor manufacturing property. Subdivision 17 covers data center computer equipment bought by June 30, 2011, subject to a $75 million investment and 100 jobs. Subdivision 18 covers computer equipment, enabling software and related hardware for data centers in Virginia localities from July 1, 2010 to June 30, 2035, if investment and job thresholds are met (lower in distressed localities) under a memorandum of understanding with the Virginia Economic Development Partnership Authority; operators must file annual reports. Subdivision 19 extends subdivision 18 to June 30, 2040 or 2050 for operators meeting larger investment and job levels, including $35 billion and $100 billion investment thresholds. The Department publishes a biennial report on the data center exemption.

notes: The document is the full section (subdivisions 1-21), although registry metadata says subdivisions 17-19; relations and entities cover the whole text. Session-law history (1993 c. 310 through 2023 cc. 144, 671, 678) is text evidence but names no registry target, so it is not coded as relations. Subdivision 12 states an end date of July 1, 2024, and subdivision 2 states that the sunlight or wind equipment exemption expires June 30, 2027; both clauses appear unchanged in the text. Subdivisions 17 and 18 have overlapping purchase periods (from July 1, 2010) with different qualifying criteria. The closing note says the list of session-law chapters may not be comprehensive.

obligations.summary: Before claiming the subdivision 18 exemption, a qualifying person, including a data center operator on behalf of itself and its tenants, must enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Virginia Economic Development Partnership Authority setting out capital investment and job determination, timelines, and repayment obligations.
obligations.applies_from: Prior to claiming the subdivision 18 exemption

evidence.quote: Prior to claiming such exemption, any qualifying person claiming the exemption, including a data center operator on behalf of itself and its tenants, must enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Virginia Economic Development Partnership Authority

obligations.summary: Annual report to the Virginia Economic Development Partnership Authority, on behalf of itself and participating tenants, covering employment levels, capital investments, average annual wages, qualifying expenses, tax benefit, and other information the Authority determines relevant, in the prescribed format.
obligations.applies_from: Annually while the subdivision 18 exemption is claimed
obligations.conditional_on: Data center operator is claiming an exemption under subdivision 18

evidence.quote: such operator shall be required to submit an annual report to the Virginia Economic Development Partnership Authority on behalf of itself and, if applicable, its participating tenants

obligations.summary: The Department of Taxation, with the Virginia Economic Development Partnership Authority, must publish a biennial report on the subdivision 18 exemption (aggregate data, tax benefit, return on investment analysis) and submit it to specified legislative committee chairmen; the Authority must share annual report information with the Department. Non-disclosure limits on aggregated data apply.

evidence.quote: The Department, in collaboration with the Virginia Economic Development Partnership Authority, shall publish a biennial report on the exemption

obligations.summary: To qualify for the subdivision 19 extension, a data center operator must enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Virginia Economic Development Partnership Authority setting out capital investment and job details, qualifying localities, and timelines.

evidence.quote: To qualify for an extension pursuant to this subdivision 19, a data center operator shall enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Virginia Economic Development Partnership Authority on or after January 1, 2023

obligations.summary: Subdivision 18 reporting requirements continue to apply to a data center operator for the duration of any extension granted under subdivision 19.
obligations.applies_from: For the duration of any extension granted under subdivision 19

evidence.quote: The reporting requirements set forth in subdivision 18 shall continue to apply to a data center operator for the duration of any extension granted pursuant to this subdivision 19.
